summary.headline: Shyam Metalics Q2 FY27 revenue rose 33.4% YoY to INR5,960 crore and operating EBITDA margin expanded 170 bps to 13.8%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue reached INR5,960 crore (up 33.4% YoY, 9.3% QoQ) on a 26% rise in sales volume to 15.49 lakh tons. Reported EBITDA was INR857 crore (14.4% margin) and operating EBITDA was INR823 crore (13.8% margin), with PAT of INR511 crore helped by a lower depreciation charge after a switch from WDV to straight-line depreciation. Management announced a proposed 51% stake in Alom Solar Pvt Ltd, which won the Phutamura coal block (170 Mt reserves, production expected July 2027), and an MoU for a 9 MTPA Maharashtra steel complex that management said is a post-FY29/FY30 decision. Capex to date is INR9,921 crore (about 53% of INR18,785 crore plan), with INR8,864 crore still to be deployed over 2 to 3 years from internal accruals.

segments.name: Carbon steel flat products
segments.commentary: Sales volume more than doubled YoY to about 81,500 tons in Q2. The HR and flat mix is scaling up, with the 1.6 Mt HR mill at Jamuria targeted for 2028.

segments.name: Stainless steel
segments.commentary: Volume grew 20.7% YoY to about 29,850 tons and realisation rose 35.2% YoY. Management cites value-added products (specialty wires, pipes); the INR2,700 crore Odisha expansion targets March 2029, and management guided about INR1,100 crore EBITDA by FY31.

segments.name: Specialty alloy
segments.commentary: Volume rose 4.7% YoY and realisation rose 18.4% YoY.

segments.name: Aluminium
segments.commentary: Volume rose 3% YoY and realisation rose 27.7% YoY. The 18,000 tpa Sambalpur foil line was commissioned in July, taking foil capacity to about 42,000 tpa; a 60,000 tpa FRP plant is planned under the INR800 crore downstream programme.

segments.name: Carbon steel long products
segments.commentary: Volume grew modestly YoY and rose 6.8% QoQ. Mittal Corp is running at about 85% utilisation, with management citing EBITDA of about INR10,000 per ton.

guidance_outlook: Management expects value-added products to reach roughly 70-80% of mix within 2 years, with the basic-supplies share falling to about 20%.
Targets overall EBITDA margin of 14.5% or more (from the 11-12% range it has been running), with a long-term aim of 15-16%.
Stainless steel is expected to contribute about INR1,100 crore EBITDA and the SBQ business about INR1,000 crore EBITDA by FY31.
Alom Solar coal block is expected to add about INR400 crore incremental EBITDA by FY31 for an estimated INR360 crore capex (Shyam share about INR185 crore).
Maharashtra 9 MTPA project: land acquisition in 1 to 1.5 years, major execution after FY29/FY30; no major outflow expected in the next few quarters.
Targets RoE of 16% and RoCE of 24% by 2031; management says about INR3,000 crore of CWIP is not yet in returns.
capex_capacity: Capex since listing INR9,921 crore (about 53% of INR18,785 crore plan); INR6,671 crore already capitalised; balance INR8,864 crore over the next 2 to 3 years from internal accruals.
HR mill of 1.6 Mt at Jamuria, targeted for 2028; auto-steel specialty bar/combo mill of 0.8 Mt at Kharagpur (INR900 crore).
Stainless steel expansion of INR2,700 crore at Odisha with downstream processing and SBQ plant, targeted for commissioning by March 2029.
Aluminium foil capacity of 18,000 tpa commissioned in July at Sambalpur; a 1.5 Mt beneficiation plant at Sambalpur (INR150 crore) was also commissioned.
Solar plant of about 9 MW commissioned at Jamuria; NCLT approved merger of Shree Venkateshwara Electrosteel Castings into Shyam Sel Ltd (tax benefit over INR15 crore).
demand_pricing: World Steel Association projects flat global steel demand in 2026 and 1.7% growth in 2027; India demand expected to grow 7.9% in 2026 and 8% in 2027.
Management said there is a shortage of HR in India at present.
Aluminium pricing was supported by Middle East disruption that has shut some plants, along with stronger domestic and export demand for foil.
Management attributed higher raw material costs to a pass-through in steel prices as demand rose, rather than cheaper inputs, when asked about raw material cost falling to about 71% of revenue.
Management said it is not concerned about new coated-steel capacity from players such as BMW Industries, which it describes as a converter business.

qa_highlights.question: Which volume drivers are expected over the next 6 to 12 months, given the sponge iron and stainless steel plants?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the revenue-driving mix will not change much near term, but expects value-added products to reach about 70-80% of the mix within 2 years as HR, stainless steel, specialty alloy and SBQ capacity comes up.

qa_highlights.question: What is the scale and timing of the 9 MTPA Maharashtra steel MoU (INR50,000 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is at an early stage. Land is expected in 1 to 1.5 years, engineering takes about 6 months, and the project will be built in phases of 4.5 to 5 Mt, with major execution after FY29/FY30. It will be 100% owned by Shyam Metalics.

qa_highlights.question: Why are margins higher in stainless steel, specialty alloys and aluminium foil this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited strong demand, a shift to value-added products (specialty wires and pipes in stainless), continuous improvement as the plant stabilises, and Middle East disruption supporting aluminium foil demand.

qa_highlights.question: How will capital allocation work between West Bengal and Maharashtra under the internal-accrual policy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are no current plans for a second Bengal phase until existing projects stabilise, and no major Maharashtra outflow in the next few quarters. It does not intend to add debt, and any shortfall of INR400-1,000 crore is manageable.

qa_highlights.question: Which segment has the best margin and how is capital being prioritised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said stainless steel earns about INR13,000-15,000 per ton EBITDA, carbon steel about INR6,000-7,000 per ton, and aluminium about INR40,000 per ton on a smaller base. It will not concentrate capital in one product.

qa_highlights.question: How is Mittal Corp performing since acquisition and what are its per-ton economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity utilisation is about 85%, with wire and bright bar exports started. Management estimates RoCE above 20-25%; the CFO corrected EBITDA per ton to about INR10,000. No major long-product expansion is planned there.

qa_highlights.question: Is new coated-steel competition from players such as BMW Industries a margin risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not worried. It views BMW as a converter, says the market is growing, and argued that full backward integration from ore to colours is the differentiator.

qa_highlights.question: Why did raw material cost fall to about 71% of revenue when peers reported increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said raw material prices have risen and the increase has been passed through to customers, with demand also rising. It noted some advantage from input prices in the growing segments.

risks_watch: Execution risk on INR8,864 crore of remaining capex, including HR mill (2028), Odisha stainless (March 2029) and Alom Solar coal block (July 2027 target).
Stabilisation of newly commissioned stainless steel and aluminium foil capacity; management says the margin gains are not from one specific factor.
Competitive intensity in coated steel and HR as new capacity (including from West Bengal players) comes on stream.
Maharashtra project is at MoU stage with land and mining not yet secured; management says no major outflow in the next few quarters.
Sustainability of margin gains if raw material prices stay volatile; a 1 pp operating margin move is material against the 13.8% base.
Sustaining RoE/RoCE progress toward 16%/24% by 2031 as CWIP of about INR3,000 crore is commissioned.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volumes, margins and balance sheet, with a strong focus on the capex programme. Management was evasive on specifics: it gave no capex timeline or cost breakdown for the Maharashtra project and offered only "nothing very specific" on the margin drivers, while routinely deferring to later periods.
key_quotes: Amit, we will not see a major change on the revenue-driving mechanism, what is going right now.
So the initial investment is going to be only for 4.5 million to 5 million tons.
We are not doing any major expansion in Mittal Corp. in the long product, because we feel like we have to invest more on the downstream rather than upstream.
We don't put everything in one basket at one time.
So presently, for next few quarters, I don't see any kind of major financials outflow coming out in Maharashtra project, because we are at a very initial stage.

adds.what: 18,000 tpa aluminium foil line at Sambalpur (foil capacity to about 42,000 tpa)
0.8 Mt auto-steel specialty bar/combo mill at Kharagpur
INR2,700 crore Odisha stainless steel expansion with downstream processing and SBQ plant
60,000 tpa aluminium FRP plant under INR800 crore downstream programme
Alom Solar Phutamura coal block (170 Mt reserves), proposed 51% stake, production expected July 2027
9 MTPA Maharashtra steel complex (MoU; post-FY29/FY30 decision)

growth.why: Management targets volume growth of 20-25% every year and an EBITDA margin of 14.5%+, backed by a INR18,785 crore capex plan (about 53% spent, INR8,864 crore to deploy over 2-3 years), with the Odisha stainless expansion and Jamuria HR mill due in 2028-2029 and utilisation near 85%; near-term capacity additions are modest, so the backing is partial.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Operating EBITDA margin rose 170 bps YoY to 13.8% in Q2 and management targets 14.5%+ overall (from 11-12% running), with stainless ~INR13,000-15,000/t and aluminium foil ~INR40,000/t EBITDA, though management was vague on drivers and raw material pass-through is volatile.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Capacity utilisation is near 85%, 18,000 tpa Sambalpur foil line was commissioned in July, and Alom Solar coal block targets production July 2027, but the major additions (HR mill 2028, Odisha stainless March 2029) fall outside the 2-4 quarter window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 sales volume rose 26% YoY to 15.49 lakh tons, management targets 20-25% annual volume growth, and carbon flat volumes more than doubled to about 81,500 t, though near-term mix is expected to stay broadly unchanged.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is about 85% and INR8,864 crore of the INR18,785 crore plan is still to deploy over 2-3 years, but management said no second Bengal phase until existing projects stabilise and the Maharashtra outflow is not expected in the next few quarters, so new approvals are more likely later.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: H1 FY27 operating EBITDA rose 41.9% YoY to INR1,588 crore and Q2 PAT jumped 96% YoY, but guidance was framed as long-term 14.5%+ margin and 16%/24% RoE/RoCE by 2031 rather than near-term upgrades.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Margin gains are tied to newly commissioned stainless and foil capacity that still needs to stabilise, and raw material prices are volatile; a 1 pp margin move is material against the 13.8% base.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Value-added mix is targeted at 70-80% within 2 years, with specialty wires and pipes in stainless, and a 60,000 tpa aluminium FRP plant is planned under the INR800 crore downstream programme.

rows.label: Alom Solar coal block (Phutamura, 170 Mt) production
rows.why: Alom Solar coal block production expected July 2027, adding about INR400 crore incremental EBITDA by FY31 for about INR360 crore capex (Shyam share about INR185 crore).

rows.label: Merger of Shree Venkateshwara Electrosteel Castings into Shyam Sel
rows.why: NCLT has approved the merger, with tax benefit over INR15 crore; no new cost-saving quantum was disclosed.

rows.label: Internal-accrual funded capex with no new debt
rows.why: Net debt is only INR192 crore and operating cash flow was INR1,544 crore in H1 FY27, with management saying it does not intend to add debt to fund the INR8,864 crore balance capex.

tone.note: Management was confident on volumes, margins and balance sheet, but evasive on the Maharashtra project timing and cost and on the specific margin drivers; analysts pushed on the raw material cost fall to 71% of revenue, BMW coated-steel competition and capital allocation between Bengal and Maharasht
